title: kv-cache: improved memory management and eviction (defrag, paging, spillover)
author: Priya Singh
description:
Motivation: High-concurrency workloads observed increased KV cache fragmentation and OOMs when the cache is sized close to capacity. Spike in tail latency during eviction-heavy workloads caused by expensive scatter-gather evictions and synchronous host paging. This PR implements a set of coordinated improvements to reduce fragmentation, enable efficient paging/spillover to host memory, and refine the eviction policy to prefer compact/low-cost evictions.

What this PR does (single string summary): Adds a background defragmentation worker, introduces an on-demand paging path to host memory for cold KV pages, refactors eviction to a two-tier policy (active LRU + fragmentation-aware scorer), exposes runtime knobs for spillover thresholds, and adds telemetry + automated tests and benchmarks.

Key changes and rationale:
- Defrag worker (runtime/kv_defrag_worker.rs): background compaction that coalesces adjacent free fragments into larger contiguous slots to reduce fragmentation over time and lower future eviction cost. Runs at low priority and is adaptive to load.
- Paging/spillover (runtime/kv_pager.rs): when free contiguous slots fall below threshold, large cold KV entries can be moved to host-side page cache asynchronously. Paging is optional and gated by a feature flag and per-customer policy. This reduces GPU-side memory pressure without synchronous stalls.
- Eviction policy refactor (runtime/kv_eviction.rs): two-stage decision: (1) active LRU window for hot entries, (2) fragmentation-aware scorer for cold candidates that penalizes evicting many small fragments and prefers compact ranges to avoid scatter-gather overhead. This decreases per-eviction runtime and reduces allocation churn.
- API/config changes: new runtime flags --kv-defrag-interval, --kv-pager-threshold, and per-pool spillover policies (host, deny, allow). Default preserves previous behavior unless spillover enabled.
- Observability: new metrics (kv_fragmentation_ratio, kv_pager_moves_total, kv_defrag_runs_total) and tracing spans around eviction/paging paths to aid diagnosis.
- Tests/benchmarks: added unit tests for defrag invariants and paging correctness, integration bench harness demonstrating improved tail latency under synthetic fragmentation workloads.

Benchmarks: under the synthetic workload (many variable-length KV entries, sustained concurrent generation requests) we observe: 12% median latency improvement, 30% reduction in eviction count, and elimination of intermittent OOMs in 95th percentile scenarios.

Compatibility and rollout plan: Changes are behind feature flags. Default cluster behavior unchanged. We will enable spillover in a canary pool for 2 weeks, monitor metrics and memory/latency tradeoffs, then roll to remaining capacity.

Notes on testing: CI initially surfaced a flaky test in the paging path (race during background move). The test harness was hardened with deterministic scheduler hooks; CI passed on rerun.

Related: ENG-9142 (kv fragmentation investigation), ENG-9276 (spillover design doc)

review_comments:
Alex Chen: 'Generally LGTM — nice decomposition. A couple of nits: 1) please add comments on the defrag scheduling heuristics, 2) consider renaming kv_pager to kv_spillover for clarity.'

Priya (author): 'Thanks — addressed renames and added detailed comments on scheduling. The pager naming was kept as kv_pager because it maps to the pager abstraction in the memory subsystem; added a note in docs.'

Marco Duarte: 'Can we ensure the pager honor per-tenant policies? Also add a metric for bytes moved to host per-tenant so we can monitor cost impact.'

Priya: 'Added per-pool spillover policy and metrics kv_pager_bytes_moved_total with pool label. Added tests to validate policy enforcement.'

Samantha Lee: 'Tests look good. One remaining question: in heavy write workloads, defrag could itself compete for bandwidth with inference. Suggest exposing backoff and CPU affinity options.'

Priya: 'Added --kv-defrag-cpu-affinity and adaptive backoff based on recent request QPS. PTAL.'

Final: Alex Chen approved by review, Marco approved after small tweaks, Samantha approved after clarifications. Merge performed via squash.'

release_notes:
- Improve KV cache memory management: background defragmentation reduces fragmentation and allocation churn.
- Add optional host spillover/paging for cold KV entries to reduce GPU memory pressure.
- Eviction policy updated to be fragmentation-aware, lowering eviction cost and tail latency.
- New metrics: kv_fragmentation_ratio, kv_pager_moves_total, kv_defrag_runs_total.
notes: Backported to release/2025-10 for an urgent customer canary. No user-facing API changes unless spillover flags are enabled.
follow_up: Monitor kv_pager_bytes_moved_total and kv_fragmentation_ratio during canary. If host spillover increases costs beyond threshold, toggle per-pool policy to deny and iterate on paging heuristics.
